LESSON: PAINTING AND COLLAGE

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.2: Painting and Collage
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Painting and Collage, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: Why is tonal variation important in painting? 2. How is texture achieved in a painting and collage picture?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Painting and Collage together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: will be developed as the learner explores multiple perspectives of painting using

varied tools and materials for creativity.

• Digital literacy: The learner uses digital technology to source virtual or actual pictures of players executing skills in football

and painting artwork.

• Creativity and imagination: The learner will apply creative skills in selecting media for painting, and painting the still life

composition.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner works on art work and clears up after the activities

• Unity: The learner practise tuning the fiddle in turns

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Waste management: developed while disposing of the waste after the classroom activity.

• Social cohesion: The learner work in groups to watch actual or virtual painting and discuss

Suggested learning resources

Water based colours, drawing papers, black sugar papers, found materials for collage, support (carton box/cardboard/ any other),

adhesive, football.
